notes: SPRINT-22 adoption, full scope in one sprint (docs/LANGUAGES.md Kotlin section): all eleven passes enabled -- the EIGHTH full-scope pack, opening wave-3. The pinned fwcd/tree-sitter-kotlin v0.3.8 grammar (the canonical community grammar; npm binding tarball sha256-verified byte-identical to the git tag for parser.c/scanner.c/node-types.json/grammar.json/LICENSE; LANGUAGE_VERSION 14 accepted by the vendored runtime v0.27.2) ships an external scanner (src/scanner.c: automatic semicolons, string-interpolation start/end/content, nested multiline comments, the safe-navigation token) that oc_add_grammar picks up automatically. Symbols: function_declaration WITH a function_body -- free functions, methods, extension functions (the receiver lives inside the receiver type, so the declaration's only direct simple_identifier is the name), generic/suspend/inline functions; body-less declarations (abstract/interface members) are NOT symbols (the C prototype discipline; Kotlin has no prototypes so every real definition carries a body). Lambdas and anonymous functions are anonymous constructs: NOT symbols, decisions count inward. Property accessors with a real body ARE symbols (the C# SPRINT-14 accounting-hole precedent: named Prop.get/Prop.set). Parameters: the field-less parameter node (name = direct simple_identifier, type = the first type child, default = an anonymous '=' token); vararg collapses to the '...' marker (the parameter_modifiers sibling shape, probed). Decision table: if_expression (else-if nested), when_entry (EVERY arm counts including else -- the Rust match_arm precedent), for_statement, while_statement, do_while_statement, catch_block, elvis_expression (the C# '??' op precedent as its own node kind) and the two boolean containers conjunction_expression/disjunction_expression (Kotlin has NO shared binary_expression; as kinds each named node counts once per occurrence -- identical semantics). Resolver v1-kotlin: the DECLARED-FACT resolver -- Kotlin's package model is decoupled from the file system (no package==directory rule, none is invented), so every specifier resolves against the RECORDED package_header clauses (the Go package_clause hint channel) and top-level declaration names (the C# namespace-hint channel, fed by the exports loop) of the analyzed set; wildcard 'a.b.*' fans out over the package's files (the Java asterisk-marker precedent), single 'a.b.C' requires the declared symbol (the union fans out over every file that carries it -- set semantics, lexicographic order), member 'a.b.C.f' matches BOTH declared-fact readings (the ambiguous member shape keeps a NULL bind -- whole-file claim, the C++ include discipline). Without hints every specifier stays unresolved (the honest degradation). The imports relation is a SET. NO mate marking (the C/C++ precedent; link order is not a parse fact). OC005 marking: wildcard claims mark whole files (fail-open); named claims mark the matching export. Entry points: EMPTY manifest list BY DESIGN -- the entry claim is the PARSE FACT of a top-level function DEFINITION named main (the Q_KT_MAIN fact, source_file-anchored so a member 'fun main' claims nothing -- probed). Test conventions: none registered in v1 (no runner-executed Kotlin convention is name-pinned). OC007 fires with a Cobertura-shaped XML via --coverage (Kover emits JaCoCo-compatible XML; the Kover XML reader is out of scope v1 -- the gcovr/SARIF-tier honesty applies: nothing is invented for a format the reader does not take). Supply tier (the honest delineation, SPRINT-22): Kotlin has NO canonical dependency manifest reader in v1 -- OC009 and OC010 are enabled pack data but nothing is ever discovered for them: gradle build files are not pins (a plugins block is not a version-pinned artifact and libs.versions.toml is a catalog, not a lockfile -- and neither is read), the KOTLIN pack contributes zero manifest rows and on a Kotlin-only scan the supply block is ABSENT with zero manifests (on a mixed scan the block may carry the OTHER packs' tiers -- the Java gradle reader on a gradle-based tree -- while the Kotlin contribution stays zero), no OSV ecosystem exists for Kotlin imports and none is invented. Metaprogramming (reflection, delegation, compiler plugins, DSLs) is a parse fact only as far as the grammar sees it -- the Rust macro boundary, accepted in the over-report direction for OC006. As-written analysis: no build-system evaluation; gradle/Ktor variants are reported as the single parsed configuration. The pinned grammar's known boundary: an in-range when_condition cannot FOLLOW an expression when_condition entry (fwcd v0.3.8, measured and classified at the corpus gate); one-line class bodies produce zero-width MISSING automatic-semicolon nodes (the external scanner requires the newline -- real source always uses them).
